factual.note: #1 proposes a taper of ZCG and Coinholder Grants funding to the 2032 halving, with the rest going to the NSM.

The thread places a boundary at 2028: ZIP 1016 payments run until then (#12), the program ends at that boundary unless reauthorised (#24), and #1 compares funding to the 2028 halving. What is decided then is not spelled out.

novel_claims.note: No post proposes quarterly milestone reporting as a condition on the taper. Nearest are conditional release by coinholder vote (#53, #58) and the question of how to measure ZCG's record (#49, #69, #77).
novel_claims.span: One option I have not seen raised in this thread: keep the taper proposed in #1, but make it conditional on ZCG publishing, every quarter, how many milestones were approved, paid and missed, with the ZEC amounts for each.

novel_claims.note: Claims such reporting would give the 2028 decision an evidence base. Nobody in the thread has said this.
novel_claims.span: That would let the 2028 decision rest on numbers rather than impressions, whichever way it goes.

repetitions.note: Backing the taper (c5) was first made at #1 and repeated at #11, #42, #44, #72. Answered at #3, #4, #9, #52 (it misses the point) and #39 (premature). This draft backs it only with a condition attached.
repetitions.span: I would support the taper with that condition attached

repetitions.note: Partly related to c16 (a conditional subsidy), first made at #7; conditional-release versions at #53 and #58 rest on coinholder votes. #63 calls that better than the current structure but unlikely to pass. No post proposes reporting as the condition.
repetitions.span: make it conditional on ZCG publishing, every quarter, how many milestones were approved, paid and missed, with the ZEC amounts for each

findings.summary: The draft proposes making the taper in #1 conditional on quarterly ZCG reporting of approved, paid and missed milestones, and says it would back the taper only on that condition. No post in the thread proposes that condition; related conditional-release ideas appear at #53 and #58. The references to #1 and to a 2028 boundary match the thread, and no tone issues were found.
